perf.summary: Find the lowest set bit v with BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount instead of a linear scan, and hoist 1<<v.
perf.currentCost: For every mask in [1,2^n), an inner loop scans i=0..n until the first set bit is found (up to n iterations + branch each), recomputing 1<<i each step. This runs ~2^n times.
perf.proposedChange: int v = System.Numerics.BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount((uint)mask); int vbit = 1 << v; int maskWithoutV = mask ^ vbit. mask is always >=1 here so TrailingZeroCount is well-defined (input nonzero).
perf.rationale: Replaces an O(n) branch loop with a single tzcnt/ctz instruction under Burst, removing a variable-length dependency chain from the hot per-mask path; also caches 1<<v.
perf.risk: TrailingZeroCount on uint 0 returns 32, but the loop starts at mask=1 so the argument is always nonzero — safe. uint cast harmless since mask<2^n with n<=30 is positive. adj index (long)v*n+u can also drop to int v*n+u (n<=30 -> <2^31), shaving the 64-bit multiply.
